research_concepts: PULL_UP jumper as a counter to PNR
play-type possession records derived from play-by-play
unit-level lift in points per possession (PPP)
league-wide consistency of an effect across units
methodological_questions: What is the unit of analysis (team-season, defender-season, or possession-type cell), and how is lift defined against a matched baseline?
How is a PNR fail defined without using the outcome of the counter possession (to avoid outcome-derived labels)?
What sample size per unit is needed to estimate lift precisely enough to judge a >2pp median threshold and a >=70% positive-share threshold?
How are shot quality, defender matchup, and game context controlled so that lift is not confounded with the type of possession?
Is the consistency criterion (>=70% of units with lift>0) corrected for multiple units and for sampling noise in each unit?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned zero records (n_results=0), so no earlier study by this project is available for this question, its concepts, or its methods.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP is a counter to PNR failure in any unit, league-wide or otherwise.
Whether the stated thresholds (>=70% of units with lift>0, median lift>2pp) are reasonable or have been tested before.
Any feasible unit definition, baseline, or effect-size estimate from prior work.
own_inferences: The question as posed does not define the unit, the lift baseline, or the PNR-fail and PULL_UP labels, so it cannot be tested exactly as written; it needs a pre-specified operationalisation.

The conditional wording ("If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real counter") is a hypothesis about a conditional response, so the test must compare PULL_UP outcomes after PNR failure against matched non-PULL_UP outcomes after the same PNR failure, not against all possessions.

Play-type possession records built from play-by-play (initiator, play type, points) can supply PNR and PULL_UP labels, but points are the outcome, so using them to define PNR failure would create outcome-derived labels.

2025-26 playoffs are partial as of 2026-05-23 (complete only from 2026-06-21), so they must be excluded from this analysis date. 2025-26 regular season is also partial before 2026-04-13 and must be excluded if the analysis is run on 2026-05-23.
Whether a league-wide positive share is informative depends on the number of units; with few units the 70% threshold is noisy, and with many small units most lifts may be near zero and sign-random.
uncertainties: Unit definition (team, defender, lineup, or possession context) is not specified.
Exact PNR-fail and PULL_UP definitions in the play-by-play and graph records are not given; the glossary and data catalog were not consulted.
Expected shot-quality and defensive-matchup differences between PULL_UP and alternative actions are unknown.
Whether the derived possession records were validated against the raw play-by-play is not stated.
No prior estimates of lift size exist in the retrieved record set, so the 2pp threshold is unanchored.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so no prior finding, failed approach, or prior answer was available to change the decision. The decision rests only on the task statement and the data description, and it is to proceed only after the design below is fixed.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR failure and PULL_UP labels must be defined without using the counter-possession points, or the lift is partly built into the label.
PULL_UP shots differ from other PNR-counter actions in shot quality, distance, and defender matchup; without matched controls lift reflects shot selection, not the counter.
Per-unit PULL_UP-after-PNR-fail samples may be small for many teams or defenders, so unit-level lift estimates may be too noisy to judge the >2pp median and the 70% positive share.
Season-to-season changes in pace, shooting, and play-type frequency across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may shift lift baselines unless seasons are modelled separately.

prior_work.summary: No earlier study was returned by retrieve_history (n_results=0), so the question cannot be marked as answered or unanswered by prior work. Whether it has been answered elsewhere is unknown.

risks.text: If PNR failure is defined using the points scored on the subsequent possession, the 'counter' lift is partly circular.
PULL_UP possessions after PNR failure differ in shot distance, shooter quality, and clock; lift must be compared with matched possessions.
Unit-level lift estimates with small denominators will be dominated by noise; the >=70% positive-share criterion is sensitive to how many small units are included.
Play-type labels (PNR, PULL_UP) from automated play-by-play classification may be misclassified; label accuracy is not established.
Testing the counter across many units and several thresholds increases the chance of a spurious positive share.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 seasons without season effects can produce lift that reflects league-wide scoring changes.
If the baseline PPP of PULL_UP is high relative to alternatives, lift can be positive even with no counter-specific effect.
No placebo or falsification check is defined in the question, so a positive result cannot be separated from generic offensive gain.
Possessions split across the 2025-26 partial data window or misattributed initiators would bias unit assignment.

design.estimand: Within-unit difference in PPP between PULL_UP possessions and matched non-PULL_UP possessions, both occurring after a PNR failure, averaged over units; the claim is supported if lift>0 in at least 70% of units and the median lift exceeds 2pp.
design.unit: Team-season (offence side of PNR failure) as the primary unit; defender-season as a secondary unit. Units must have at least a pre-specified minimum number of PNR-fail possessions.
design.sample: NBA regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 (complete). 2025-26 regular season only if the analysis is run after 2026-04-13 (complete). 2025-26 playoffs excluded at 2026-05-23 (partial). Playoff seasons analysed separately if included at all.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum per-unit sample (e.g., at least 40 PNR-fail possessions per unit with PULL_UP or matched alternative) and compute the bootstrap CI of each unit's lift; report the share of units with CI excluding 0 and the probability the 70% share holds under resampling. Power to be checked by simulation before analysis.
design.controls: Match PULL_UP and alternative counter possessions on shot distance, shooter tier, defender matchup, clock, score margin, and season; estimate lift with season fixed effects and a random effect for unit. PNR-fail defined from pre-counter events only (e.g., defender switch, screener-defender not recovering), not from counter points.
design.falsification: Run the same lift calculation for a placebo action with no hypothesised counter role (e.g., a non-PULL_UP shot type after PNR success). Also test whether the lift is positive in the first half versus second half of each season. If the placebo shows comparable lift, the counter claim is not supported.
design.multiplicity: Fix the 70% and 2pp thresholds before analysis; apply a false-discovery correction across unit-level tests if individual units are reported; treat the league-wide share as the single primary test.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) the share of units with lift>0 is >=70%, (b) the median lift exceeds 2pp, (c) the placebo lift is not comparable, and (d) the result holds in at least two of the three complete regular seasons. Rejected if the share or median falls below threshold with adequate power. Otherwise report as uncertain.
design.data_version: Frozen extract as of 2026-05-23: 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs complete; 2025-26 regular season excluded unless run after 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs excluded (partial). Record the exact play-by-play and graph-database build used.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
